evidence: The samples for the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) observations were prepared as described earlier.14 The specimens were observed in a HRTEM (Hitachi: H9000NAR) operating at 300 kV . To investigate the composition of the interfacial layer, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was applied. The binding energy scale was calibrated for each measurement with the C 1 s signal from C–C bonds at 285.0 eV . For electrical characterization, aluminum gate electrodes with an effective area of 0.204 mm 2 and thickness of 100 nm were e-beam evaporated through a shadow mask onto the ZrO 2 film surface. The backsides of the substrates were HF etched prior to the deposition of continuous aluminum electrode in order to create ohmic contacts. Al/ZrO 2 /native SiO 2 /n-Si(100)/Al and Al/ZrO 2 /n-Si(100)/Al capacitor structures thus created were measured with a HP 4284A precision LCR meter and Keithley 2400 source meter to obtain capacitance–voltage (C–V) and current–voltage (I–V) characteristics, respectively. All electrical measurements were carried out at room temperature. For the C–V measurements the voltage step was 0.05 V and the frequency of the ac signal was 100 kHz–1 MHz. For the I–V measurements stair sweep voltage with the step of 0.05 V was applied. Some of the samples were postdeposition annealed in forming gas (95% N 2 ,5 %H 2) at 400 °C for 30 min. The thickness, roughness, density and crystal structure of as-deposited ZrO 2 films were evaluated by x-ray reflectometry and by grazing incidence x-ray diffraction (GIXRD) using a Bruker D8 Advance x-ray diffractometer.
